title: 4D Chicago Source
description: One bibliographic source, one file. The filename stem is the source_id.

date.description: Publication or creation date as written on the source.

describes_date.description: The date the source DESCRIBES, when different from when it was made. Wau-Bun was published 1856 and describes 1831; that gap is the whole reason this field exists.

archived_url.description: Required for type=website and for any online-only source. A citation that cannot be re-read is not a citation.

locator.description: Page, plate, scan page, or IIIF region. Cite the specific place, not the whole volume.

tier.description: 1 period/eyewitness · 2 near-primary recollection · 3 compiled secondary (Andreas) · 4 later scholarship · 5 modern retrospective illustration/reconstruction · 6 decorative/popular cartography. Tiers 5-6 inform inventory and cross-checks only; never sole evidence for documented, never traced for geometry.

rights_status.description: check_required and restricted block asset derivation; textual citation stays allowed.

rights_checked.description: Fill when moving check_required to cleared or restricted.

asset_use.description: How far this source may be used. 'geometry' permits tracing; 'orientation' permits toponyms and rough placement only.

verified.description: True only when a human or agent has actually retrieved and read this source at its locator.

access_notes.description: Fetch problems worth recording, e.g. hosts that return 503/403 to automated retrieval.

what_it_supplies.description: What this source can legitimately be used FOR. Fill it in when a source is commonly misused, so an agent reaching for it sees the limit before the citation.

what_it_does_not_supply.description: What this source is often assumed to give but does NOT. Hathaway 1834 is the motivating case: it is widely described as showing individual buildings and it does not, a claim that reached this project's own brief before anyone opened the scan at full resolution.

work.description: The document this page carries, named as it is printed on the page — publication, date and, where the page gives them, the witnesses speaking.

date.description: The document's own date, as written on the page. Not the date the page was fetched.

tier.description: The rung THIS document sits on. The record's own tier is the best rung declared here — a modern site hosting an 1883 interview is worth what the interview is worth, and nothing about the hosting improves or spoils it.

note.description: Which of this project's claims the document carries, or why it is here at a rung it does not lift the page to.

transcribes.description: What a modern page transcribes, when the record dates its own retrieval rather than a document. A tier is a judgement made once, and until this field existed the judgement lived in a sentence in `note` that no check could read: `chicagology_kinzie_bridge` said 'Tier 3 for the Andreas transcription; the surrounding apparatus is a finding aid' and nothing held the 3 to the Andreas. Required for such a record graded at tier 3 or better (`tools/validate.py` § check_transcription_declarations); optional and still checked above it.

carries_no_document.description: The reading — not a flag — that established that this page was opened and reprints no document: what was looked for, what is actually printed there, and where the page sends you instead. The third state beside `transcribes` and silence, and it exists because the first two cannot tell a page that was read from a page nobody has opened. A record declaring this may not be graded at or above the testimony rung: there is no document on the page for the rung to be a judgement about. Mutually exclusive with `transcribes`, and only meaningful on a record that dates its own retrieval.
